correctness.rationale: Block multiplication reduces the commutator to a_i B_j−a_j B_i. Arrange a_i as m×r matrix A; each of c matrices Y_j must make A Y_j^T symmetric. If rank A=d, Gaussian elimination gives exactly d(m−d)+d(d−1)/2 independent constraints, leaving m(r−d)+d(d+1)/2 entries per Y_j; central coordinates contribute cm. Rank-d matrices form irreducible bases of dimension d(m+r−d), giving affine kernel bundles and the exact Gaussian-binomial sum in every characteristic. I independently enumerated six finite q,m,r,c configurations from the actual brackets, all matching the formula. When m=r=2, A≠0 is irreducible dim5c+4 and A=0 is affine dim6c. For c≤3 any prescribed Y tuple has nonzero A0 solving ≤3 equations in four unknowns; A=tA0 approaches A=0, proving irreducibility. For c≥4 dimension comparison proves exactly two components. This is a structural argument, not finite extrapolation.
